sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The window is a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue was flat at 0.2% growth in FY2023, then rose 125.9% in FY2024, 114.2% in FY2025 and 65.5% in FY2026 [D284][D338][D393][D448].
The FY2024 step came from Data Center revenue up 217% on Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P22][P23].
FY2026 growth was driven by data center compute and networking platforms, with Blackwell the majority of Data Center revenue [P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
Within it, Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and networking grew 142% on NVLink for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Operating income grew 60.1% against revenue growth of 65.5%, an incremental operating margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Operating costs grew 24.8pp slower than revenue in FY2026, at 40.7% [D476][D468].
Diluted EPS rose 66.7% against net income growth of 64.7%, with the diluted share count down 1.2% [D452][D450][D470].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 sits well above the 32.8% window median but below the 62.4% FY2025 high and far above the 15.7% FY2023 low [F50][D813][D812][D811].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1% as cost of revenue grew 91.4% against revenue growth of 65.5% [D462][F30][D465][D448].
The FY2026 operating margin slipped 2.0pp, with cost of revenue a 3.9pp drag partly offset by R&D and SG&A at 1.3pp and 0.6pp [D463][D477][D478][D479].
In FY2026 net margin of 55.6% sat 4.8pp below the 60.4% operating margin, despite $11.1 billion of other income [F70][F50][D861][X120].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income, below the 0.97x window median and the 0.86x window low [F100][F60][D435][D851][D850].
Free cash flow of $96.7 billion was a 44.8% margin, against a 44.4% window median and a 46.6% FY2025 high [F110][D432][D822][D821].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A, up from 1.74x in FY2025 [F105][D431][D437][D382].
Investing outflows of $52.2 billion rose on higher equity investment purchases and a non-exclusive license agreement with Groq [F120][P1].
Cash and investments of $43.2 billion against total debt of $8.47 billion left net cash of $34.7 billion, or 26.6% of revenue in FY2025 [D384][D440][D386][D387].
The FY2026 net-cash figure is not comparable: short-term investments were not reported in FY2026 though reported in FY2025, so the pack omits them and the values built on them [R3].
Return on average equity of 101.5% ranks at the 100th percentile of six semis peers against a 20.3% median [D447][D848][D849].
Buybacks of $40.1 billion plus dividends of $974 million were 42.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 1.2% [X150][X160][D444][D470].
Short-term investments were not reported in FY2026 though reported at $34.6 billion in FY2025, so net cash and cash and investments for FY2026 omit them [R3][X188].
This is a data gap rather than a deterioration, but it makes the FY2026 net-cash comparison and peer rank unusable until the line is filed.
Graphics was 44.1% of revenue and fell 25.0% in FY2023, a one-period decline [D753][D754][R1].
The segment has since recovered to $22.5 billion of FY2026 revenue, so the flag reads as cyclical rather than structural [S125].
Whether gross margin holds above the 71.1% FY2026 level or falls further as cost of revenue grows faster than revenue, in the FY2027 10-K [F30][D465][D448].
Whether operating cash flow to net income recovers above the 0.97x window median from 0.86x, in the FY2027 10-K [D435][D851].
Whether Data Center revenue growth stays above the 68.2% FY2026 rate or decelerates, in the FY2027 10-K [D621].
